title: bug: baselineRun tests assume NT symlink privileges and POSIX process groups on native Windows
description:
Fresh approved full gate for task-05e1f916f49c44eb97c08ca3f0e6e542 failed in native Git Bash: baselineRun.test.ts:72 fs.symlink EPERM; :101 U3 assessment timeout exceeded 5000ms. Log /tmp/moe-account-switch-05e1-final-gate.log (2026-10-25T11:59:37Z, exit1): daemon 4106 passed, 2 failed, 16 skipped.
U1 creates a file symlink without a capability guard on this non-elevated host; U3 calls runAssessment whose terminateTree uses negative-PID POSIX signals, while the driver explicitly rejects win32 and other POSIX-only tests are guarded.
Resolve the native test portability/safe fixture coverage (or authorize an appropriate verified gate environment) so the required gate can run; do not weaken Linux process-tree/symlink coverage. This must land before the account-switch row can complete; no dependency on that row.
definitionOfDone: Native Windows daemon suite no longer fails on baselineRun U1 EPERM or U3 timeout, using explicit capability/platform handling consistent with the POSIX-only driver contract.
POSIX/Linux tests retain real symlink and assessment-timeout coverage with fresh passing evidence; no leaking detached assessment process after the Windows path.
Provide fresh targeted native Windows and POSIX test output plus exact modified paths.

implementationPlan.description:
Test-only fix in packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/baselineRun.test.ts (LF, keep LF). baselineRun.ts stays READ-ONLY: production never reaches runAssessment on win32 (checkPreconditions refuses win32 first) and the driver contract is POSIX-only.

1. Import mkdtempSync, rmSync, symlinkSync next to existsSync from 'node:fs'.
2. Split U1 'reads bounded regular receipts, skips malformed lines and links without echoing content' (line 69) into:
   a. it('U1 reads bounded regular receipts, skips malformed lines and directories without echoing content') = the same body MINUS the fs.symlink line (72); every other line/assertion byte-identical.
   b. directly after it, a module-level sync probe in the style of `runnable` (line 192), with a comment that an NT file symlink needs SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege (elevation or Developer Mode) and POSIX always runs the link case:
      const canSymlink = process.platform !== 'win32' || (() => { const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-symlink-probe-')); try { symlinkSync(path.join(dir, 'target'), path.join(dir, 'link'), 'file'); return true; } catch (e) { if ((e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EPERM') return false; throw e; } finally { rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } })();
      The short-circuit is what keeps Linux coverage: POSIX never probes, so a Linux symlink failure FAILS the test instead of skipping it.
      Error handling: only EPERM (missing privilege) maps to false; every other error is rethrown so test collection fails loudly instead of skipping; the finally removes the probe dir on every path.
   c. it.runIf(canSymlink)('U1 never follows a receipt symlink'): temp() dir, write one.jsonl = JSON.stringify(receipt()) + '\n', fs.symlink(one.jsonl, link.jsonl), then expect(await readUsageReceipts(dir)).toEqual({ rows: [receipt()], malformedLines: 0, notes: [] }).
3. U3 'assessment timeout preserves not-run and a null exit' (line 101) becomes it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')(...) with a one-line comment: terminateTree signals POSIX process groups; on win32 process.kill(-pid) throws ESRCH, so a hung assessment is never killed and outlives the run (the driver refuses win32). Body unchanged. skipIf(win32), not runIf(linux): macOS keeps it.

Do NOT touch: the first U3 test (passes natively, never hangs), U5 and its guards, E1-E6, U6, any timeout value.

Red proof (Linux only, throwaway copy built with the step-2 (A) snapshot recipe): in the COPY's baselineRun.ts change the readUsageReceipts filter `f => f.isFile() && f.name.endsWith('.jsonl')` to `f => (f.isFile() || f.isSymbolicLink()) && f.name.endsWith('.jsonl')`; `npx vitest run src/benchmarks/baselineRun.test.ts -t U1` must FAIL 'U1 never follows a receipt symlink' (notes non-empty: O_NOFOLLOW refuses the link). Delete the mutated copy. (Architect observed exactly this, 2026-10-26.)

Never rerun the UNMODIFIED file on native Windows: its U3 timeout leaks a hung held-out tree (mem:gotcha-baseline-native-windows-gate); the red is already on record in /tmp/moe-account-switch-05e1-final-gate.log.

- Ownership: only the test file is yours. Never stage or revert peers' dirty paths.
Fix any finding, then rerun step 2's (A) and (B) before moe.complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: test-only explicit guards. An EPERM capability probe (win32-only, POSIX short-circuits to true) plus it.runIf for the split-out link case; it.skipIf(win32) on the U3 timeout, mirroring U5 and checkPreconditions' win32 refusal.
Rejected:
(1) runAssessment refusing win32 in production: production never reaches it on win32 (checkPreconditions throws first); it would drop the first U3 test's passing native coverage; and it changes an exported function to fix a test defect.
(2) taskkill /T /F tree-kill in terminateTree: contradicts the POSIX-only driver contract and needs its own Windows evidence.
(3) Raising the 5s timeout: the hang is unbounded (terminateTree is a no-op on win32) and leaks the tree.
(4) A try/catch around fs.symlink inside the test: passes silently without link coverage; runIf reports an honest skip.
(5) A junction, like the workloadSnapshot tests use: junctions link directories only, and readUsageReceipts' case is a file link.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Measured on this host's Windows node v24.16.0:
- process.kill(-pid, 0) throws ESRCH. signalGroup returns false, terminateTree returns false without signalling, and boundedCommand awaits proc.done forever.
- fs.symlinkSync(...,'file') throws EPERM.
- fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK are undefined, so readBounded degrades to O_RDONLY; the rest of U1 passes natively.
Precedents: U5 skipIf(win32) (lines 129/139); the module-level sync `runnable` probe (line 192); workloadSnapshot.test.ts:725 platform-guards its file symlink.
tsconfig.json excludes src/**/*.test.ts, so only the explicit tsc command type-checks this file.
The in-tree node_modules has win32 bindings only. /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5 holds a lock-equal Linux install.
The architect prototyped this exact change in throwaway copies: Linux 14 passed / 6 skipped (E-tests: no dist); native Windows 10 passed / 10 skipped, 0 held-out processes, no new temp dirs. The follow-symlink mutation fails the new link test.
planningNotes.risks:
- A guard that could skip on Linux would silently weaken coverage. The short-circuit prevents it; prove it with ✓ in run (A).
- Do not reproduce the Windows red: it leaks a hung node --test tree. If a held-out process ever appears, kill only your own, fingerprinted by exact PID + CreationDate + CommandLine (mem:gotcha-baseline-native-windows-gate). Never kill a broad node tree.
- Windows interop: run from a Windows-drive cwd, never a UNC /tmp cwd, and strip MOE_*/CLAUDE* (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl).
- The shared checkout has 500+ foreign dirty paths: overlay only the owned test file into snapshots, and commit nothing (the wrapper lands).
- task-05e1f916 (account switch) is BLOCKED on this task through its reason text and auto-unblocks at DONE; no dependency edits are needed.
